COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPMS No. 1900 of 2018
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Present Mr. Vipul Sharma, counsel for 
the petitioner.
Present Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, Brief 
Holder for the State/respondent nos. 1 & 2. 
Present Mr. Sudhir Kumar, counsel for 
the respondent no. 5.
None is present for other respondents.
2. Counsel for the petitioner would submit
that there was an order of Debt Recovery 
Tribunal, whereby possession of the property 
in question was to be handed over to the 
petitioner; that, the court receiver was 
appointed and he was directed to file the report 
by taking the assistance of the police; that, the 
court receiver in paragraph 3 of his report 
(annexed as Annexure No. 4 to the writ 
petition) stated that the concerned S.D.M. 
never intended to assist the undersigned and 
on every date they cooked different story and 
delayed the proceeding from one pretext to 
another. Initially all employee of the S.D.M. 
office including S.D.M. was saying that the 
said property cannot be identified, demarcated 
and taken over physical possession as the 
same is small part of big area of land owned 
by one dabang family of this area.
He would further submit that in his 
report the court receiver further stated that the 
concerned S.D.M. again shown their inability 
for execution of the Order of the Hon’ble 
Tribunal and direction of the concerned D.M. 
as the property belong to a person namely 
“Babby”, who is very affluent person of the  society and having political connections.
3. The then Assistant Collector, Bazpur (as 
he then was) District Udham Singh Nagar i.e. 
respondent no. 2 is directed to file counter 
affidavit on all facts including the report of 
court receiver.
4. The said affidavit be filed within two 
weeks from today.
5. List this matter on 08.01.2024.
 (Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 08.11.2023
Akash

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPMS No.1900 of 2018
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Mr. Vipul Sharma, learned counsel for the
petitioner. 
2. Mr. Yogesh Tiwari, learned Standing 
Counsel for the State. 
3. Mr. Sudhir Kumar, learned counsel for 
respondent no.5.
4. Mr. Teerath Pal Singh, Addl. Chief 
Executive Officer, Smart City, Dehradun (the then 
Assistant Collector, Bazpur) and Mr. Rakesh 
Tiwari, Assistant Collector, Bazpur are present in 
person. 
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner/auction
purchaser would submit that the petitioner is the 
auction purchaser of the land in question in 
pursuance of an order passed by the Debt 
Recovery Tribunal, Delhi; that, the Court receiver 
was appointed and a direction was given to the 
Collector to provide assistance to the Court 
receiver for transfer of possession to the 
petitioner/auction purchaser; that, the Court 
receiver filed a report to the effect that hardly any 
assistance was provided by the Assistant Collector, 
Bazpur at that time rather he told the receiver that 
there is an influential person named Bubby and it 
is difficult to get the possession delivered to the 
petitioner/auction purchaser. 
6. Mr. Teerath Pal Singh, Addl. Chief 
Executive Officer, Smart City, Dehradun, who was 
the Assistant Collector, Bazpur on the relevant 
date and time would submit that revenue case 
No.22/16 of 2013-14 was filed by respondent no.5 
against the respondent no.4 in respect of the same 
land wherein status quo order had been passed on 
08.08.2014 by his predecessors.  7. To this, learned counsel for the 
petitioner/auction purchaser would submit that as 
per the Section 18 of the Recovery of Debts and 
Bankruptcy Act, 1993 “no court or other authority 
shall have, or be entitled to exercise, any 
jurisdiction, powers or authority in relation to the 
matters specified in section 17”. 
8. He would further submit that Section 34 of 
this Act also says that the provisions of this Act 
shall have effect notwithstanding anything 
inconsistent therewith contained in any other law, 
therefore, the proceedings of Case No.22/16 of 
2013-14 were not maintainable, therefore, if at all 
there was any status quo order that was of no legal 
consequence in view of the decree passed by the 
Debt Recovery Tribunal. 
9. Learned counsel for respondent no.5 would 
submit that Sections 18 and 34 of the Recovery of 
Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993 are not 
applicable in the present case. He prays for and is 
granted time to place law on this point. 
10. Mr. Teerathpal Singh, the then Assistant 
Collector, Bazpur is directed to file additional 
counter affidavit stating all the details in respect of 
the request made by the petitioner/auction 
purchaser or the receiver and the action taken on 
that request before the next date of listing. 
11. Put up on 21.03.2024.
 
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 14.03.2024
BS

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPMS No. 1900 of 2018
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Present Mr. Vipul Sharma, counsel for 
the petitioner.
Present Mr. Yogesh Chandra Tiwari, 
Standing Counsel for the State.
Present Mr. Kirti Sharan Agarwal, proxy 
counsel for Mr. Sudhir Kumar, counsel for the 
respondent no. 5.
2. Mr. Tirth Pal Singh, Addl. Chief 
Executive Officer, Smart City, Dehradun (the 
then Assistant Collector, Bazpur) and Mr. 
Rakesh Tiwari, S.D.M., Bazpur are present in 
person.
3. Response affidavit filed by Mr. Tirth Pal, 
the then Assistant Collector, Bazpur dated 
20.03.2024, is taken on record.
4. Counsel for the State would submit that a 
letter was sent to the receiver even prior to the 
report of the receiver requesting him to get the 
petitioner impleaded in the revenue 
proceedings but there was no response on the 
part of the S.D.M. However, the moot 
question is that the order of Debt Recovery 
Tribunal, Delhi despite all other litigations 
was executable or not and whether no 
assistance was provided to the receiver as 
stated in his report.
5. In the interest of justice, present S.D.M., 
Bazpur is directed to take appropriate steps for 
implementation of the order of D.R.T in 
question if it is executable in the eyes of law 
after taking all the legal opinions on that point 
and to file status report on the next date of 
hearing. 6. Counsel for the petitioner and private 
respondent no. 5 would submit that they may 
be permitted to supply the copies of the order 
and the law in their support to the present 
S.D.M., Bazpur.
7. The present S.D.M., Bazpur would 
submit that for preparation of the Lok Sabha 
elections, he is appointed as an A.R.O. as well.
8. List this matter on 27.06.2024.
9. Personal appearance of the concerned 
officials is hereby exempted.
 (Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 21.03.2024
Akash
